Thermite fits wherever a change can be measured. If a program can build your project, run it and say whether the result is right and how good it is, agents can try ideas on it for days, and Thermite's **judge** keeps only what it confirms. The same harness serves very different people. Pick the page that sounds like you.

## What you can point it at

Every campaign is one of three **modes**. Each use case below uses all three.

| You want to | Mode | For example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Push one number as far as it goes, without breaking anything else | Hill climb | Tokens a second on your GPU, a build's time, a query's latency, a model's accuracy |
| Make something work, checked by a list of goals | Goal | Support a new model format, pass a test suite after an upgrade, meet a quality bar |
| Find out what is known, with sources you can check | Research | Which papers improve 2-bit decoding; which library fits a design |

[Choose a campaign mode](../how-to/campaigns/choose-a-mode.md) helps you pick one.

## The proof

[Qwen3.8-27B on a $100 GPU](../studies/qwen3-8-27b-on-a-p100.mdx) is a study of four campaigns on one Tesla P100: two goal campaigns, then two hill climbs. Decode went from 7.74 to 30.06 tokens a second with the model's outputs held, and the result ships in one command through [tensorless](https://tensorless.dev).
